stem: How does the manual define a PRINCE2 practice?
answer: An area of project management that has to be addressed in the same way at every point of the project's lifecycle
distractors: A step in the project lifecycle that is performed once at a defined point
A role within the temporary project management team
A management product that records the information needed to manage the project
A principle that the project board must continually reinforce
A technique for planning and controlling the delivery of products
A theme that runs through the processes but may be omitted on small projects
explanation: A practice is an aspect of project management that has to be addressed consistently across the whole lifecycle, and it needs specific treatment for the processes to be effective. A principle is a guiding obligation, a role is a responsibility and a management product is information, so none of them fits this definition.

stem: Which list contains all seven PRINCE2 practices?
answer: Business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress
distractors: Business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, change and progress
Business case, people, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress
Benefits, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress
Business case, organizing, plans, assurance, risk, issues and progress
Business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, stakeholders and progress
Business case, directing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress
explanation: The seven practices are business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress. Change is a management approach rather than a practice, people is a separate element of the method, and directing is a process.

stem: Which pairing of a PRINCE2 practice with the question it answers is correct?
distractors: Business case — What?
Quality — Why?
Organizing — What now?
Progress — Who?
Issues — What if?
Risk — Where are we now?
explanation: Plans answers how the work will be done, how much it will take and when, while the business case answers why, quality answers what, organizing answers who, risk answers what if, and issues answers what now. Progress asks where we are now, where we are going and whether to carry on.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 need an organizing practice rather than relying on normal line management?
answer: Because projects are cross-functional, so accountability, delegation and delivery must be assigned within a temporary team that represents business, user and supplier interests
distractors: Because line managers are not permitted to fund any project work
Because the project board must approve every appointment to a project role
Because suppliers sit outside the organization and cannot be managed
Because the project manager reports to the business layer rather than to line managers
Because project roles are permanent and must be resourced by the business
Because the executive must delegate all delivery work to the senior user
explanation: Organizing sets out who directs, who manages and who delivers, and defines the roles, responsibilities and relationships of the temporary team so that business, user and supplier interests are all represented. It exists because cross-functional project work does not fit the normal line management hierarchy.

stem: The project board wants to know whether the plan can still be achieved and whether the project should continue. Which practice provides this, and on what does it rely?
answer: Progress, using a mixture of event-based and time-based controls to monitor performance and escalate deviations
distractors: Plans, using the stage plan and team plan to show how the objectives will be met
Issues, using the issue register to respond to deviations from the plan
Quality, using quality control activities to confirm that products meet their criteria
Business case, using benefits reviews to confirm that the investment is still worthwhile
Risk, using the risk register to show whether exposure remains within tolerance
Organizing, using role descriptions to confirm who is accountable for performance
explanation: Progress addresses the ongoing achievability of the plans, monitoring performance and escalating when events do not go to plan through a mixture of event-based and time-based controls. It ultimately determines whether and how the project should proceed; the business case justifies the investment but does not control progress.

stem: What does the manual identify as the particular strength of PRINCE2 in relation to the seven practices?
answer: The way the seven practices are integrated, both in how they link together and in how they are used across all the processes
distractors: The way each practice can be applied in isolation by a specialist team
The way the practices replace the principles when a project is tailored
The way each practice has its own management product and technique
The way practices may be omitted on small or simple projects
The way the processes describe the practices in more detail than the practice chapters do
The way the practices are applied only at stage boundaries
explanation: The strength of PRINCE2 is the integration of the seven practices, linked to one another and used across all the processes. The processes describe the progressive flow of the project and call on the practices when they are needed, while the practice chapters supply the detailed guidance.

stem: Through what mechanism are the practices principally applied and tailored?
answer: A suite of management approaches, each defining the procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities for that aspect of project management
distractors: A set of product descriptions, each defining the quality criteria for a product
The project mandate, which records the business's initial requirements
The daily log, which records informal actions and events
A tailored set of principles, one for each practice
The project plan, which defines the stages and their tolerances
A role description for every member of the temporary team
explanation: Each management approach, such as the benefits management approach, sets out the procedures, techniques and standards to be applied and who is responsible, which is how a practice is made fit for the project. Product descriptions, role descriptions and plans are management products, not the mechanism for applying a practice.

stem: What does PRINCE2 prescribe about how a management approach is documented, and who decides?
answer: Nothing is prescribed about format, level of detail or publication; the project board establishes the level and type of documentation it needs within agreed business policies
distractors: A single reference document is required, approved by the executive before initiation
A comprehensive instruction manual is required for every practice on every project
The project manager chooses the format, and the board approves it at each stage boundary
The programme office prescribes the format, and the project may vary only the content
PRINCE2 provides a template for each approach, which may be shortened but not restructured
The senior supplier decides the format, because the approaches form part of the contract
explanation: PRINCE2 deliberately leaves documentation open, from a few paragraphs to a comprehensive instruction manual, because the board must decide what it needs in order to manage and document its decisions. What varies is the level and type of documentation, not whether the approach exists.

stem: A small, low-risk project team proposes to drop two practices because the project is simple. What is the manual's position?
answer: All seven practices should be applied; they vary only in how they are applied, according to scale, risk, people, organizations and complexity
distractors: Practices may be dropped if the project board records the decision in the project log
Practices may be dropped on projects that are not part of a programme
Only the practices that have management products need to be applied
Practices may be replaced by equivalent techniques from the chosen delivery method
All seven must be applied with the same degree of formality on every project
A practice may be dropped only if its tolerance has been set to zero
explanation: The manual states that all seven practices should be applied in a project, while the way they are applied varies with scale, risk, the people and organizations involved, and complexity. That variation keeps the method consistent with the seven principles; it is not a licence to omit a practice.

stem: Which two management products does the manual single out as relevant to the majority of the practices?
answer: The project initiation documentation and the project log
distractors: The business case and the risk register
The project plan and the stage plan
The project brief and the end project report
The communication management approach and the lessons log
The product register and the quality register
The project mandate and the benefits management approach
explanation: Chapter 4 introduces the project initiation documentation and the project log because most practices either contribute to them or draw on them. The business case, the plans and the individual registers are components of these products or sit within the project log.

stem: The project initiation documentation, together with the stage plan, is described as what?
answer: The 'contract' between the project manager and the project board
distractors: The contract between the customer and the supplier
The agreement between the programme and the project
The baseline for the end project report
The mandate authorizing the project to start
The terms of reference for project assurance
The approval record for each stage boundary
explanation: The project initiation documentation gives the direction and scope of the project and, alongside the stage plan, forms the contract between the project manager and the board. Commercial contracts with suppliers are separate arrangements, and the mandate comes before the documentation rather than being part of it.

topic: The PID as a living product
stem: How is the project initiation documentation kept current, and what happens to the version that authorized the project?
answer: Its components are reviewed for currency at the end of every stage and re-baselined if needed, while the authorizing version is preserved as the basis for assessing performance at closure
distractors: It is frozen at the end of initiation and replaced by the stage plan for each stage
It is rewritten at each stage boundary, and the previous version is discarded
It is updated continuously, and the latest version replaces the authorizing baseline
It is reviewed only at project closure, when the end project report supersedes it
Only the business case within it is updated, because the rest was approved once
It is re-baselined at closure so that reported performance matches the plan
explanation: The documentation is a living product that should reflect the current status, plans and controls, so each component is reviewed for currency at every stage end and changed in a structured way if required. The baseline version used to gain authorization is always preserved, because it is the reference against which performance is later assessed.

stem: What is the purpose of the project log?
answer: To keep a live record of issues, lessons, products, quality, risk and other actions or events, covering both current and past activity
distractors: To describe how the project will be directed, managed and delivered
To provide the single source of reference about the project for people joining it
To record the board's decisions and the tolerances it has set
To hold the baseline version of the project initiation documentation
To list the management approaches and the responsibilities for each
To summarize the project's performance for the end project report
explanation: The project log is dynamic, holding the current and historic record of issues, lessons, products, quality, risk and other formal or informal actions. It may be a single document or, more commonly, a collection of logs and registers; being the single source of reference for new joiners is a use of the project initiation documentation.

stem: A team wants to replace product-based planning with its own scheduling method. What does the manual say about substituting techniques?
answer: PRINCE2-specific techniques cannot simply be substituted, because omitting or replacing one requires the method to be tailored, whereas additional context-specific techniques may be omitted or substituted freely
distractors: Any technique may be substituted provided the project board approves the change
Additional techniques may be substituted only if a PRINCE2-specific technique is retained in their place
All techniques are optional, because techniques are guidance rather than part of the method
Substitution is permitted only where the project uses an agile delivery method
Only the project manager may substitute a technique, and only at a stage boundary
Techniques may be substituted if the change is recorded in the project log rather than the project initiation documentation
explanation: Each practice chapter describes two kinds of technique: those specific to PRINCE2, such as product-based planning, and additional ones that are useful depending on context. The additional techniques can be dropped or swapped without affecting how PRINCE2 is applied, but changing a PRINCE2-specific technique is a tailoring decision.

stem: Which of these is NOT one of the standard sections of a PRINCE2 practice chapter?
answer: The tolerance thresholds that the practice sets for each project objective
distractors: The purpose of the practice
The techniques that support the practice
The focus of key roles for the practice
explanation: A practice chapter follows a set structure: purpose, guidance, techniques, applying the practice, management products, focus of key roles and key relationships with the principles. Tolerances are set for the project as a whole and described within the relevant approaches, not as a standard section of every practice chapter.
